questions.q: The table summarizes measurements from a aerodynamics evaluation (LINALG-969538453); using these entries, for the two-way table above. If one participant from Lab 1 is chosen at random, what fraction corresponds to outcome Positive?
questions.answer: **Answer:** C. There are \(19\) participants in Lab 1 (\(13 + 6\)), of whom \(13\) recorded Positive, giving \(\frac{13}{19}\).
questions.explain: There are \(19\) participants in Lab 1 (\(13 + 6\)), of whom \(13\) recorded Positive, giving \(\frac{13}{19}\).

questions.q: The accompanying figure illustrates a acoustic chamber configuration (LINALG-G919206596); using it showing four contiguous class intervals in a frequency histogram. How many total observations are recorded across all four bars?
questions.answer: **Answer:** C. Summing bar heights directly from the histogram gives \(3 + 9 + 9 + 4 = 25\).
questions.explain: Summing bar heights directly from the histogram gives \(3 + 9 + 9 + 4 = 25\).

questions.q: From the plotted structural truss figure above (LINALG-G935984215) showing a rectangle with labeled side lengths. Compute its area.
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. Reading length \(12\) and width \(4\) from the rectangle, area \(= 12 \times 4 = 48\).
questions.explain: Reading length \(12\) and width \(4\) from the rectangle, area \(= 12 \times 4 = 48\).

questions.q: The table summarizes measurements from a flow bench evaluation (LINALG-885650358); using these entries, evaluate \(f(g(3)) + 4\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. From the table, \(g(3) = 4\) and \(f(4) = 12\). Adding \(4\) yields \(12 + 4 = 16\).
questions.explain: From the table, \(g(3) = 4\) and \(f(4) = 12\). Adding \(4\) yields \(12 + 4 = 16\).

questions.q: Given the measurements marked directly on the turbine profile schematic (LINALG-G902428977) showing region cardinalities for sets \(A\) and \(B\) inside a universal sample space. Using the Venn regions, find \(|A \cup B|\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** B. Counting each disjoint region once yields \(|A \cup B| = 10 + 3 + 9 = 22\).
questions.explain: Counting each disjoint region once yields \(|A \cup B| = 10 + 3 + 9 = 22\).

questions.q: The accompanying figure illustrates a antenna pattern configuration (LINALG-G852096120); using it showing a sinusoidal wave with dashed midline \(y = 5\) and labeled peak. What is the peak-to-trough range (maximum minus minimum)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. From midline \(5\) to peak \(7\), amplitude is \(A = 7 - 5 = 2\), so peak-to-trough range equals \(2A = 4\).
questions.explain: From midline \(5\) to peak \(7\), amplitude is \(A = 7 - 5 = 2\), so peak-to-trough range equals \(2A = 4\).

questions.q: Inspect the robotics values listed across the table (LINALG-868872739); representing a quadratic polynomial \(q(x)\) with equally spaced inputs. Determine \(q(4)\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. First differences are \(6, 14, 22\), giving constant second difference \(8\). Thus \(q(4) = 48 + 30 = 78\).
questions.explain: First differences are \(6, 14, 22\), giving constant second difference \(8\). Thus \(q(4) = 48 + 30 = 78\).

questions.q: Consider the upper-triangular matrix \( W = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 19 \\ 0 & 8 \end{pmatrix} \). Determine the eigenvalue product \( \det(W) = \lambda_1 \lambda_2 \).
questions.answer: The eigenvalues are \( 4 \) and \( 8 \), with product \( 32 \).
